content.title: About
content.content: Veal chop is a cut of meat from a young calf (usually 3–6 months old), taken from the loin or rib section. The meat is light pink, tender, with a mild flavor and relatively low fat content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Veal is considered a leaner meat compared with beef because of its lower fat content.
Veal chops are featured in classic French and Italian dishes such as "Veal Milanese" and "Veal Piccata".
Because the meat is tender, it cooks quickly – pan‑searing, grilling, or baking to medium doneness keeps it juicy.
In some countries calves are raised on milk‑based diets, which gives the meat a delicate taste.
Veal is rich in heme iron, making it an excellent source of easily absorbable iron.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Veal provides complete protein needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with beef, veal contains less saturated fat, which is better for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: It supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, essential for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Iron and zinc
items.content: The heme iron in veal is readily absorbed, and zinc supports immunity and wound healing.

items.title: Creatine source
items.content: Veal naturally contains creatine, which can help improve muscle strength and endurance.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked veal may harbor harmful bacteria such as Salmonella. Cook to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C (145 °F).

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rarely, individuals may experience allergic reactions to meat proteins.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Like other red meats, veal contains purines, which can exacerbate gout symptoms.

items.title: Hormones and antibiotics
items.content: Choose certified products to avoid residues of growth hormones or antibiotics.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Veal chops can be pan‑seared, grilled, or baked. Lightly pounding the chop ensures even thickness. Serve with vegetable sides, wine‑based sauces, or creamy reductions. Thinly sliced veal works well in salads and sandwiches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep veal refrigerated at 0‑4 °C and use within 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Thaw in the refrigerator, not at room temperature, before cooking.
